[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Using JSON Extractor and XPath Extractor in JMeter"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When performing API performance testing with Apache JMeter, you often need to capture dynamic values (such as auth tokens, session IDs, or transaction IDs) from a server response and pass them to subsequent requests. This tutorial covers how to use two of the most powerful Post-Processors for this task: the JSON Extractor and the XPath Extractor."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. The JSON Extractor"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The JSON Extractor is used when your server responds with JSON data. It uses JSONPath expressions to parse the response and extract values into JMeter variables."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Add a JSON Extractor: Right-click your HTTP Request sampler, hover over "Add", select "Post-Processors", and click "JSON Extractor"."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Names of created variables: Define the variable name you want to use later, for example, "auth_token"."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"JSONPath Expressions: Define the path to the element, such as "$.data.token"."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Match Numbers: Set to "1" to capture the first occurrence, or "-1" to capture all occurrences into an array."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"Example JSON Response:
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": {
    "token": "abc123xyz456",
    "userId": 789
  }
}

JSONPath Expression: $.data.token
Variable Name: auth_token"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"2. The XPath Extractor"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"The XPath Extractor is used when your application responds with XML or HTML documents. It evaluates XPath expressions against the response to extract specific nodes or attributes."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Add an XPath Extractor: Right-click your sampler, go to "Add" -> "Post-Processors" -> "XPath Extractor"."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Tidy / Use XPath2: Check "Use XPath2" for modern XML/HTML processing or use Tidy for lenient HTML parsing."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reference Name: The variable name to store the extracted result, e.g., "session_id"."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"XPath Query: The query string to locate the element, such as "//input[@name='sessionId']/@value"."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"Example XML/HTML Response:
<html>
  <body>
    <form id="loginForm">
      <input type="hidden" name="sessionId" value="session_98765" />
    </form>
  </body>
</html>

XPath Query: //input[@name='sessionId']/@value
Reference Name: session_id"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Validating Extracted Values"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"To verify that your extractors are working correctly, always add a "Debug Sampler" and a "View Results Tree" listener to your Thread Group. Run your test once and inspect the JMeter variables tab in the View Results Tree to confirm your variables contain the expected extracted data."}]
